STYLE BLOCK 3.
Rendering: a funny flat editorial cartoon caricature. Use clear drawn shapes and a few expressive lines. This is a silly satirical cartoon, not a portrait.
Caricature: use the height, the head size, and the build that this prompt gives. Keep the complete head, hair, ears, and chin inside the stated head-height limits. Exaggerate only the named identity features without increasing the head height. Each body is adult.
Face: use one solid flat skin color on the face, ears, neck, and hands. Give the skin no shadow, highlight, blush, or tonal modeling. Draw two solid eyebrow shapes, small eyes with plain dot pupils, one nose contour, one mouth line, and at most four short expression lines. Use no iris detail, eye reflections, shaded lips, pores, stubble dots, or freckles.
Hair: use one solid silhouette and at most one broad hard-edged shadow shape. Use the same rule for facial hair. Use no strands, streaks, thin bands, or separate highlights.
Contours: one uniform dark ink line surrounds the complete outer silhouette. Its nominal width is 3 pixels per 1000 pixels of reference height. Reference height is 94 percent of the canvas height. At 1254 pixels square, use a 3.54-pixel line. Keep the same width on the head, arms, torso, and legs, for all heights and builds. Interior lines are thinner and sparse. Use no broken, sketchy, tapered, or colored outlines.
Shading: clothing and shoes use one solid base color and at most one broad hard-edged shadow shape per material. Leave large areas completely flat. Use no highlights on fabric, skin, hair, or shoes. A lens or metal fitting may have one small flat highlight. Use no gradients, soft transitions, texture, fabric weave, rim light, or glow.
Detail: use large clothing shapes and at most two short fold lines per limb. Use plain shoes without laces or seams. Use no tiny pattern, stitching, or decorative noise.
Not permitted: a realistic or semi-realistic face, lifelike skin, portrait lighting, painterly blending, a three-dimensional render, anime, a sticker border, or mixed rendering techniques.
